title: Volley Wave Event
description: Non-retained live mirror of one supervisor journal event, published to volley/_waves/<wave>/events. The envelope type is the journal event type. Event data is free-form except for the event types constrained below. See spec sections 4.6.3, 4.6.15 and 4.6.16.

wave.description: Wave id, or the pseudo-wave _system for global events.

seq.description: Journal sequence number, monotonic per wave.

task.description: A wave-file task id, or _release: the release train's pseudo task (spec section 4.6.19).

data.description: Event-type-specific detail.
The Claude account a spawn runs under and why (spec section 4.6.11), journaled right before its agent_spawned. Names no e-mail.

score.description: Its pace (spec section 4.6.12): the smallest over its windows of room left, on the projection with its agents in flight, against the time to that window's reset, in units of the window's length (1 is on pace); null with no usage data. Optional: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

binding.description: The window that sets score (the tightest decides); null with no usage data. Optional.

eligible.description: Every window it reported is under claude.balance.cap_pct on the projection with its agents in flight (spec section 4.6.12). Optional.

binding_left.description: The binding window's room left, in percent. Optional.

binding_resets_at.description: When the binding window resets; null when unknown. Optional.

in_flight.description: The agents counted against it (spec section 4.6.12): running on it, or picked for it and not yet reporting usage. Optional: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

projected_pct.description: The binding window's used percentage with each agent in flight reserving its look-ahead; null with no usage data. Optional.

decision_id.description: The agent_account_limit decision whose answer moved it (absent: an agent_move_account request).

data.description: The wave's account for its agents not yet spawned moved (spec section 4.6.11): from the account it left and to the one its new agents start under, null meaning balanced; by: who moved it.

decision_id.description: The account_limit decision the move answered (absent: a wave_account_set request no open decision offered).

from_host.description: The task's effective host before the version (`local`, `auto` or a host name).

to_host.description: The host the new version writes for it.

from.description: The host the task was placed on before, when it is re-placed.

local.description: The supervisor's own machine (its agents' tasks[].host stays absent); absent for a peer.

by.description: Who archived the wave: the owner or caller, an admin, or the supervisor (auto-archive).

closed_decisions.description: The decisions the archive closed with answer archived (each journaled before as decision_resolved).

files.description: The merged PR's files that overlap the task's; empty under nudge_on_merge: all.

on.description: What it waits on: a task of the wave, a PR, an issue (one or more).

head.description: The PR head GitHub reports CONFLICTING, where the branch-update step starts.

role.description: The role whose pushed head it is (implementer, fixup).

kind.description: fix_flake: a red head's failing test the PR does not touch (spec section 4.6.16); a dedicated fixer is requested, never a re-run.

test.description: The failing test id the fixer is for (its dedupe key).

test_file.description: The test's file, null when its id names none.

for.description: The task whose red head it is.

task.description: A flake's fixer: fix-<slug of its test> (spec section 4.6.16); a merge train: train-<n>.

data.description: A synthetic task (spec section 4.6.16): added by the supervisor, never by a wave file; issue 0, the wave's pipeline, no after. A flake's fixer carries its remediation, a merge train its members.

A flake's fixer settled (spec section 4.6.16): landed (done: merged) releases the tasks still parked on its test, which update from the release branch and are verified again; failed (cancelled, blocked, escalated) puts each blocked task's red head back to the owner, escalated unattended_safety.
The supervisor published the wave's digest on volley/_waves/<wave>/digest and pushed its one-line summary (spec section 4.6.16).
The supervisor handed an agent's dropped terminal status to its pipeline again, a while after it alarmed on it (spec section 4.6.2).

after_ms.description: How long after the status arrived it was recovered.

data.description: The supervisor holds the task for CI on sha: its runs completed and all of them (checks), and, when the head's jobs could be read, the same for its jobs with the running and failed job names (jobs) and the estimated seconds left (eta_s, absent without an estimate) (spec section 4.6.8).

The supervisor marked a draft PR ready for review at head (gh pr ready), so the CI its repository skips on drafts runs; the CI gate on that head then counts only runs created at or after at (spec section 4.6.8).
The supervisor labeled a done task's issue merged-to-release when its PR merged into the release branch (spec section 4.6.19).
The supervisor removed the merged-to-release label once the release reached the default branch (spec section 4.6.19).
The supervisor commented on a task's issue; the comment carries marker, so it is never made twice (spec section 4.6.19).
The supervisor closed a done task's issue the release PR left open (spec section 4.6.19).

The release reached the default branch in release_pr and every task's issue was checked: closed lists the issues the supervisor closed, left_open the cancelled or deferred tasks' issues it left open (spec section 4.6.19).
A wave-file task's data may carry its bundled issues, its footprint (files, footprint) and where the overlap plan put it (plan).

terminal.description: The terminal the agent runs in (fleet.local_terminal on the supervisor's own machine; tmux on a paired machine; spec section 4.6.15). Absent from a supervisor that predates it.

churn.description: The spawn is churn (spec section 4.6.16): it never spends the spawn budget. Absent: productive.

cause.description: Why a churn spawn ran: a branch update (rebase), a review round (or its fixup) a branch update caused, a merge train's spawn, or a relaunch, respawn or retry of a role in its step.

issues.description: A bundle's issues as fetched (spec section 4.6.22), the task's issue first; absent for a task with one issue.

via.description: The task merged as a member of a merge train, in train_pr.

data.description: The overlap plan for the wave's current version, its clusters as the wave state's overlap_plan carries them.
A cluster of the overlap plan changed how it runs.

churn.description: The churn fuse put the cluster on hold (spec section 4.6.16): the churn spawns of the task the event names.

data.description: A merge train started: its tasks, each one's gated head, and the release branch commit it integrates them onto.
A merge train merged in pr as merge_sha, landing every one of its tasks.
A merge train failed (a conflict integrating it, or red CI on its head); its tasks go back to the merge queue.
In _system: the roles record (volley/_system/roles) differs from the last one journaled; roles is the new record's payload.
In _system: a role move began.
In _system: one step of a role move changed status.
In _system: a role move passed its health check; the record names the new machine.
In _system: a role move failed; rolled_back says whether its automatic rollback restored the old machine.
In _system: a completed move was undone by hand (role_rollback); to is the machine the role is back on.
